newsitem.title: USA: Photos of slain Colorado child obtained by tabloid.
newsitem.headline: Photos of slain Colorado child obtained by tabloid.

text.p: The murder investigation of six- year-old JonBenet Ramsey took a strange turn Saturday when it was revealed a supermarket tabloid planned to publish autopsy photos of the beauty pageant winner.

Officials in Boulder, Colorado said an internal investigation was undertaken to determine how the photos were leaked to the Florida-based Globe and the family of the dead girl called the publication's editors "jackals, not journalists."
"The sheriff has initiated an investigation," said Boulder city spokeswoman Leslie Aaholm. She also said Coroner John Meyer believed the photos were "authentic."
The planned publication of the photos left the family of the dead girl stunned.

"The ghoulish publication of these photos by the Globe is beneath contempt. It is a callous act and poses a grave threat to the integrity of the investigation of JonBenet's murder," family spokesman Pat Korten said in a statement.
The family asked other news outlets not to republish or televise the photographs.
Boulder County sheriff's office said it did not have an immediate comment on the investigation into how the photographs were released.
The Ramseys have also directed their attorneys to "pursue all available avenues of legal recourse," Korten's statement said.
The edition with the photos is expected to be on sale Monday.

Autopsy photos are used as evidence in criminal trials. Boulder police, who have kept quiet on most details of the murder investigation, have said they do not want to disclose aspects of the case that only the killer or killers would know.
One photo expected to be published shows the murder weapon. A Denver radio talk show host Saturday suggested listeners ask their grocery store managers not to display the issue with the photos.
No suspects have been named in the Dec. 26 slaying of the little girl who was strangled and, according to published reports, sexually assaulted.
Her body was found by her father in the basement some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note on the backstairs on her way down to make coffee in the morning.

The suspected sale of the photos reflects the intense media attention that has befallen Boulder, a small college town about 30 miles (50 km) northwest of Denver. About 300 media represenatives have converged on the town.
The slaying has all the elements of a made-for-TV-movie: a ransom note, rich parents, and the child a contestant in beauty pageants.
John Ramsey is a prominent business executive and his wife Patricia a former Miss West Virginia.
